TH.name: Thailand
tipping: Restaurants: 10% service charge is often included; otherwise, leaving 20-50 THB change is customary.
Street food / local stalls: Tipping is not expected, but small change is appreciated.
Taxis: Rounding up to the nearest 10 or 20 THB is common practice.
Massage & Spas: 50-100 THB for good service is standard courtesy.
etiquette: Wai Greeting: Press your palms together at chest level with a slight bow.
Royal Family: Treat all images and currency depicting the Royal Family with utmost respect (Lèse-majesté laws).
Temples: Remove shoes before entering; dress modestly covering shoulders and knees.
Feet & Head: The head is considered sacred (do not touch someone's head). Never point the soles of your feet at people or Buddha images.
checklist: Passport with at least 6 months validity
Lightweight, breathable clothing + modest temple attire
Cash (Thai Baht) for street markets & transport

VN.name: Vietnam
tipping: Restaurants: Tipping is not strictly mandatory, but 5-10% is polite in tourist spots.
Taxis: Rounding up the fare is customary.
Tour Guides: 100,000 - 200,000 VND/day per person is customary.
etiquette: Crossing streets: Walk slowly and steadily; scooters will navigate around you.
Temples & Pagodas: Dress conservatively; remove hats and shoes when entering inner sanctuaries.
Chopsticks: Never stick chopsticks vertically in a bowl of rice (resembles incense at funerals).
checklist: Vietnamese Dong (VND) cash - cash is king for street food
Grab app installed for reliable taxi booking

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.timezone: WIB (UTC+7 in Jakarta) / WITA (UTC+8 in Bali)
tipping: Restaurants: Many add 5-10% service charge. Leaving extra 10,000 - 20,000 IDR is appreciated.
Taxis: Rounding up to the nearest 5,000 or 10,000 IDR is standard.
etiquette: Right Hand Only: Use your right hand to give or receive items and to eat; the left hand is considered unclean.
Dress code: Wear a sarong and sash when visiting Balinese temples (often rentable at entrance).
Public Behavior: Avoid loud public displays of anger or physical intimacy.
checklist: Passport valid for at least 6 months
Power plug adapter (Type C/F two-round pins)
Cash (IDR) in smaller denominations for convenience

PH.name: Philippines
tipping: Restaurants: 10% is standard if service charge is not yet included in the bill.
Taxis / Rides: Rounding up or giving 20-50 PHP extra is appreciated.
Delivery / Service staff: 20-50 PHP is polite.
etiquette: Respect to Elders: 'Mano po' (placing elder's hand to forehead) and using 'po' and 'opo'.
Friendliness: Warm smiles and hospitality are ubiquitous.
Punctuality: Account for local traffic in metropolitan cities.
checklist: Philippine Peso (PHP) cash for tricycle/jeepney fares
Powerbank & waterproof pouch for island tours
